dimensional_subject_showcase.name: dimensional_subject_showcase
dimensional_subject_showcase.description: One dimensional subject, or a small staged set of them, is held as the visual centrepiece of its own stage so that form, silhouette, surface, structure, articulation, arrangement or hidden interior becomes legible and workable, whether the subject reveals itself on its own timing, the viewer steers the viewpoint and closes in to study it, or the viewer handles the subject directly so its shape and configuration are what the region visibly carries. Fits requests for product, device, artifact, character, creature, anatomy or specimen showcases, mockup and staged-object presentations, hero centrepieces that turn, open up or invite close study, cutaway, see-through and inner-layer demonstrations, posable, adjustable or configurable staged subjects whose shaping feeds a companion area of the page, and quiet display pages whose whole payoff is understanding the shape and staging of the thing or things shown, rather than imagery presented and browsed as the subject, figures charted, a space entered and travelled, a control performing expressively, a field animating behind readable text, or authored content changing state.

ambient_decorative_surface_layer.name: ambient_decorative_surface_layer
ambient_decorative_surface_layer.description: A view is given one continuous atmospheric or decorative field that pervades it as the setting for whatever it holds — filling it, surrounding, framing or edging the content, receding behind it in depth, or registered onto the marks and words themselves — carried by motion, light, texture, optical quality, shaped geometry or layered pictorial depth, and whether it holds steady, answers the visitor's presence, or shifts through moods across the view, while the foreground it acts upon keeps its ordinary role and is never itself advanced, accumulated or turned into something else. Fits requests for atmospheric landing and splash screens, hero, intro, alert and contact panels, section backdrops, decorative edges, seams and frames around or between stacked content regions, glowing, drifting or restless surrounds for a headline, tag or supporting line, immersive reading and document views whose long text stays dominant inside a designed surround, mood-led pages carrying one continuous treatment across their prose and pictures, cinematic full-view mood scenes whose depth, framing and quiet liveliness exist to set a tone around a single short title, sampler runs whose interest lies in a family of decorative treatments applied around ordinary content, and near-empty views holding a lone mark whose payoff is the luminous, hazy, textured, deep or optical surround playing across the view, rather than a dimensional subject presented for study, imagery browsed as the subject, figures charted as the content, a place entered and travelled, a control performing expressively, something behaving on its own terms as the subject, a graphic made under the visitor's hand, or authored content visibly changing state.

presented_visual_media_viewing.name: presented_visual_media_viewing
presented_visual_media_viewing.description: Flat visual items — pictures, artwork, footage, marks or self-contained visual specimens and examples — are held as the primary foreground content and given a designed presentation for looking at and taking in, whether one item alone owns the whole view under a distinctive treatment or many peer items are traversed so each comes forward and is seen in turn before receding. Fits requests for photo, artwork and illustration showcases, galleries, portfolios and showreels, moodboards, image-led openings and single-item viewers whose one visual carries the whole message, quiet mood or display views, browsable collections of small peer items such as icons, logos, tags, thumbnails, styles or design examples gathered for looking through and comparing, and any page whose visual moment is presented visual material itself being displayed and browsed rather than a dimensional object studied for its form, figures charted, a space entered and travelled, an interface element performing expressively, a graphic being made, or a field animating behind readable text.

information_graphic_visualization.name: information_graphic_visualization
information_graphic_visualization.description: Information itself — amounts, proportions, division of a whole, trends, relationships, hierarchies or locations — is the visual subject, turned into a graphic whose shape, position, extent, connections or accompanying figures make it readable as a structure, whether it holds the whole view or a persistent region beside other content, and whether it is fixed, updating on its own, or explored, focused and reshaped by the visitor on the graphic itself. Fits requests for chart, graph and diagram features, statistic, metric and score highlights, live readouts, gauges, dials and monitoring panels, allocation, budget, coverage and capacity pictures showing how a bounded total is divided and what remains, data-storytelling and progress or growth narratives, comparison and ranking displays, map and geographic views, node-link, network, mind-map, taxonomy and entity-relationship overviews whose branching and links carry the meaning, generated answer or topic breakdowns laid out as a structure to be surveyed and drilled into, and small planning or apportioning surfaces whose working object is the information graphic, rather than a dimensional object studied for its form, imagery presented and browsed, a space entered and travelled as the content, a control performing expressively, something behaving on its own terms, a graphic made as authored artwork, authored content changing state, or a field animating behind readable text.

explorable_place_environment.name: explorable_place_environment
explorable_place_environment.description: An environment is presented as a place the visitor occupies and moves through, with the view itself acting as the interface and the surroundings remaining the primary content, whether the visitor's viewpoint travels the place directly or they are present within it as a visible figure among whatever else inhabits it, and whether they roam freely, orient toward things situated around them, or advance along a laid-out passage whose progress and direction they govern. Fits requests for illustrated or rendered scene homepages, virtual rooms, worlds and landscapes, maps-as-places, guided settings and walkthrough or tour views of a locale, spatial menus whose destinations live in the scenery, inhabited gathering places and lingering spots where simply being somewhere with others is the point, open-ended atmospheric wandering, and any page whose visual moment is a place being occupied and travelled rather than one object inspected for its form, imagery presented and browsed, figures charted, a control performing expressively, something behaving on its own terms, a graphic made under the visitor's hand, authored content changing state, or a field animating behind readable content.

expressive_interface_control_moment.name: expressive_interface_control_moment
expressive_interface_control_moment.description: An interface element — a control, affordance, indicator, status mark, overlay, card, tile or option panel — is itself the visual moment, carrying a designed reactive or self-sustaining behaviour that is the whole of what there is to see, whether it responds to being pointed at, focused or operated, or holds itself as a standing signal of the interface's state, while the surrounding content keeps its ordinary role and is never itself advanced or transformed. Fits requests for playful inputs, buttons, toggles, sliders, menus and search or send affordances given a memorable reaction, hoverable or focusable cards, tiles, rows, plan and option panels that take on emphasis, lift, unfold or bring forward their action when engaged, loading, waiting, liveness and status indicators occupying an inline region, panel or holding view, logos, badges, cursors, pointers, hints, labels and helper or explanatory overlays that visibly build, react, resolve or persist as a page is read and used, micro-interaction demos and interface experiments, and any page whose visual payoff is an interface element behaving expressively rather than a dimensional subject inspected for its form, imagery presented and browsed, figures charted as the content, a space entered and travelled, something behaving on its own terms as the subject, a graphic made under the visitor's hand, authored content changing state, or a field animating behind readable text.

visible_transition_state_change.name: visible_transition_state_change
visible_transition_state_change.description: Authored material, or the view holding it, is visibly put into a different state as the designed moment — arriving, advancing, giving way, being obscured or uncovered, restructured into an alternate presentation of the same content, or transformed away — so what the visitor registers is the content changing state and the state now in effect, whether the changeover is drawn out and watched, cycles continuously, or lands immediately with the resulting state as the payoff. Fits requests for intro, threshold and enter-the-site moments, paged and sequential reading experiences, slide, section and step transitions, reveal-on-advance storytelling, curtain, wipe, sweep and before-and-after changeovers, headline, sentence and typographic entrances, resolutions or exits, looping text and content reveal pieces, switching a body of content between distinct presentations or reading modes while it stays the same content, single-cue transition demo pages, and any page whose visual payoff is authored content visibly changing state rather than a dimensional object inspected, imagery presented and browsed, figures charted, a space entered and travelled, a control performing expressively, something behaving on its own terms as the subject, a graphic made under the visitor's hand, or a field animating behind readable content.

self_acting_reactive_subject.name: self_acting_reactive_subject
self_acting_reactive_subject.description: One self-acting or reactive subject, scene or field is the thing shown and watched, holding the view or a large bounded region of it as its dominant foreground content beside at most brief framing copy, whether it unfolds on its own timing, sustains itself endlessly without resolving, runs a course that settles into a finished resting state, or answers in its own manner to the visitor's presence, touch, placement, viewpoint or a live signal from its surroundings; any exposed affordance or viewpoint adjustment stays subordinate, tuning or re-reading the ongoing behaviour rather than making the view a system worked for an outcome. Fits requests for playful web toys and idle watchable pages, self-playing scenes and staged happenings that progress by themselves, creature, character or mascot companions that react to being approached, tactile substances and material playthings that can be poked and disturbed, abstract fields and motion pieces whose collective behaviour is itself the subject with a quality left dialable, short statement or single-idea sections whose sole illustration is such a responsive field carrying the point beside a line or two of copy, long-running ambient spectacles and screensaver-like displays whose imagery answers live conditions around them, and any page whose visual moment is something behaving as the thing shown rather than a dimensional subject examined for its form, imagery presented and browsed, figures charted as the content, a space entered and travelled, an interface element performing expressively beside ordinary content, a working system operated firsthand for the consequences it produces, a graphic made as supplied output, authored content visibly changing state, or a field animating behind ordinary readable content.

generative_visual_output_workshop.name: generative_visual_output_workshop
generative_visual_output_workshop.description: A picture is produced rather than pre-authored, and the resulting graphic itself holds the view as the outcome being generated, whether the visitor shapes it directly, supplies settings that compose it, or simply sets it going and asks for another result while the composition forms itself. Fits requests for pattern, poster, texture, palette and artwork generators, generative and algorithmic art pages that yield a fresh piece per run, canvases and surfaces that accumulate a composition, mark-making and expressive creation toys, image effect, filter and stylisation tools, avatar or identity makers, configurator stages whose output is the picture, and any page whose visual moment is a graphic coming into existence as made output rather than existing media presented and browsed, a dimensional object inspected for its form, figures charted, a space entered and travelled, an interface element performing expressively, a live field operated under continuous direct input, authored content visibly changing state, or a field animating behind readable text.

hands_on_operable_live_field.name: hands_on_operable_live_field
hands_on_operable_live_field.description: A working system, machine or field occupies the view and is worked firsthand by the visitor — through its own controls, through direct pointer and keyboard input, or by placing, linking and adjusting the working parts themselves — so the payoff is putting it into action and reading the visible consequences it produces inside itself rather than watching it or reading about it, whether it answers continuously while being driven or resolves on a deliberate command. Fits requests for small browser games, arcade interludes and timing, aim or reflex challenges, puzzles and score panels, open-ended playgrounds and sandboxes with steerable figures or loose objects, working replicas, emulators and simulated devices, appliances, instruments, panels, terminals or screens presented for the visitor to try themselves, operable players and transports that run content under the visitor's commands, composition surfaces where discrete labelled units are gathered from a catalogue and joined into a runnable assembly whose outcome shows on the parts, hands-on demo stages that let a system actually be used, and any page whose visual moment is a working thing being operated and responding rather than a dimensional subject inspected for its form, imagery presented and browsed, figures charted, surroundings entered and travelled as the content, an interface element performing expressively beside ordinary content, something behaving on its own terms without being driven, a graphic made as output, authored content visibly changing state, or a field animating behind readable text.

first_person_view_altering_overlay.name: first_person_view_altering_overlay
first_person_view_altering_overlay.description: The visitor's own field of view is the affected content: something worn, applied or looked through sits at the near edge of a full-view scene and changes how that entire view is perceived, so the visible function is experiencing a chosen or applied condition from the inside rather than inspecting the thing responsible as an object on a stage or reading a field behind ordinary content. Fits requests for try-it-on-yourself and wear-it previews, lens, tint, filter, coating, screen and visor demonstrations, look-through-a-window or through-a-surface views, vision, eyesight and perception simulations, condition previews such as light, weather or time of day applied across a whole view, and any page whose visual moment is the viewer's own view being altered by the option held in front of it, rather than a dimensional subject inspected from outside for its form, imagery presented and browsed as the subject, figures charted, a space entered and travelled, an interface element performing expressively, something behaving on its own terms, a graphic being made, authored content visibly changing state, or a field animating behind readable text.

orbit_to_inspect_settled_subject.name: orbit_to_inspect_settled_subject
orbit_to_inspect_settled_subject.description: One finished subject sits alone on a quiet, low-distraction stage and keeps its form while the visitor's vantage is the only thing that changes: dragging swings the viewing angle around it, wheel or pinch moves nearer and further inside safe limits, and motion eases or coasts back toward a resting framing, often over a slow idle turn or a re-render of the subject at each new angle. Fits requests to present a single object, product, artifact, globe, specimen, or extruded word, logo or type form as a turnable centrepiece that visitors spin, tilt, zoom and study from every side without the subject changing what it is.

particle_swarm_composed_form.name: particle_swarm_composed_form
particle_swarm_composed_form.description: The subject has no solid skin: it exists as a crowd of small drifting grains, specks or soft puffs on a near-empty field, and the payoff is watching them gather into a legible form, keep breathing in place, scatter or tear open where the pointer or an edit touches them, and stream back onto the exact contour, with the assembled form still turnable to read its depth. Fits requests for particle logos and marks, dust- or speck-formed figures and creatures that materialise out of a void, glowing point-cloud sculptures that heal after being disturbed, and typed or edited lettering built from living particulate matter.

directly_posed_articulated_figure.name: directly_posed_articulated_figure
directly_posed_articulated_figure.description: A neutral figure or articulated subject waits on a plain stage and is reshaped by dragging controls attached to its own parts, so each drag bends, swings or twists that region in real time, the affected scope is made visible, impossible or irrelevant parts are refused or damped, and one action returns it to the neutral stance while the view can still be swung around the result. Fits requests for posable characters, rigged mannequins, joint or limb handles, region-based bending and soft deformation stages, and showcases whose point is that the visitor arranges the subject's pose.

variant_swap_reshaping_subject.name: variant_swap_reshaping_subject
variant_swap_reshaping_subject.description: One persistent body of matter stands at centre and becomes whichever alternative the visitor picks from a small set of named, numbered or thumbnail choices: the same substance flows, reshuffles or sweeps into the new shape instead of cutting to it, the active pick stays readable, and the chosen viewing angle and distance survive the swap. Fits requests for shape-shifting hero forms, morph-between-variants selectors, block or voxel subjects that rebuild into another object or symbol, and single-subject stages that switch between a few named forms such as globe to flat map.

scrubbed_build_progression_subject.name: scrubbed_build_progression_subject
scrubbed_build_progression_subject.description: One continuous amount, whether a slider, a scroll position or a dragged control, maps directly onto how far the subject's own construction has gone, so the visitor drives it forward and backward through the same in-between states, from flat to finished or from whole to consumed and back, with progress readable, the state holding wherever the control stops, and orbit and zoom free throughout. Fits requests for scrub-through assembly and unfolding demos, build-up or disassembly walkthroughs, progress-driven fold and net-to-solid models, and dissolve or erosion showcases the visitor can wind either way.

turn_angle_face_handover_panel.name: turn_angle_face_handover_panel
turn_angle_face_handover_panel.description: A flat, two-faced subject hangs alone on a quiet stage and what is visible is a function of the angle it is turned to: as drag or scroll swings it, the current image thins toward an edge-on sliver and hands over cleanly to the second face or picture, it holds wherever it is left, and reversing the gesture brings the first one back. Fits requests for lenticular and dual-image panels, flip cards with a different front and back, two-sided artwork or badge reveals, and single-object rotations whose payoff is crossing from one face to the other.

pointer_window_inner_layer_reveal.name: pointer_window_inner_layer_reveal
pointer_window_inner_layer_reveal.description: The subject is shown intact until the pointer opens a travelling aperture in its outer surface that exposes the inner layer of the very same subject underneath; the opening follows the pointer, its size or softness can be adjusted, and it closes and heals behind as the pointer moves on or stops, while the subject may keep turning under it. Fits requests for x-ray, cutaway, see-through and inner-structure reveals, brush- or lens-away skin removal, and anatomy or internals demonstrations driven by where the visitor points.

self_animating_inhabited_subject.name: self_animating_inhabited_subject
self_animating_inhabited_subject.description: The staged subject is alive on its own: it, or a small creature or agent travelling over its surface, keeps moving continuously without prompting, clinging to and visibly marking the form it crosses, while the visitor watches, orbits, or briefly holds and lifts it to study the contact closely, and the ongoing motion resumes exactly where it was suspended. Fits requests for showcase objects with a wandering critter or mascot, idle-animated toy or robot characters on a plinth or floating platform, surface-crawling agents that answer to the form's contours, and hold-to-inspect stages whose life continues after release.

pointer_trailing_luminous_stroke_field.name: pointer_trailing_luminous_stroke_field
pointer_trailing_luminous_stroke_field.description: A quiet, otherwise undisturbed view in which the visitor's pointer or finger becomes a drawing tool: a self-lit stroke — rope, ribbon, strand, spark shower, droplet chain, painted dot trail or a bright streak cut into the backdrop — is emitted at or dragged behind the contact point, lagging, thickening and brightening with speed, then decaying, coiling or fading back to nothing within seconds after movement stops, leaving the ground, headline and content exactly as they were. Fits requests for glowing cursor trails, cursor-painted light ribbons and paint strokes, elastic rope, tail and strand followers, meteor or spark cursors, liquid droplet trails, and light-writing traced over a big title or statement, where the trail itself is the whole effect and a click or tap at most restyles or flings that same trail.

pointer_deflected_drifting_field.name: pointer_deflected_drifting_field
pointer_deflected_drifting_field.description: One continuous field of repeating drifting elements — luminous bands and ribbons, fine linework, patterned texture, or a floating layer of small shapes — that moves on its own and answers pointer or finger proximity by locally bending, swelling, gathering or lifting near the contact point with distance falloff and a soft lag, then relaxing back into its own drift by itself once the visitor leaves. Fits requests for interactive backdrops whose existing pattern reacts where you hover, hover-attracted or hover-repelled line and particle fields, drifting light bands that lean toward the cursor, and shape layers that rise into a travelling bulge over a wordmark, where nothing is deposited and the field's resting drift always returns.

pointer_bulged_lettered_surface.name: pointer_bulged_lettered_surface
pointer_bulged_lettered_surface.description: A view whose own lettering-bearing plane behaves as a soft sheet or stretched membrane: wherever the pointer travels the surface itself swells into a smooth rounded bump beneath the words, lifting, enlarging or relighting the letters riding the crest, and it smooths perfectly flat again the moment the pointer moves away, leaving no trail or residue. Fits requests for oversized type printed on a squishy or stretchy sheet, headline surfaces that bulge, dent or ripple under the cursor, and single-question or single-wordmark views whose whole effect is the deformation of the printed plane rather than anything added on top of it.

pointer_carried_light_reveal_field.name: pointer_carried_light_reveal_field
pointer_carried_light_reveal_field.description: A view resting well below its lit state until a light the visitor carries passes over it: a pool, spotlight or backlight fixed to the pointer relights, unmasks or recolours whatever it reaches — mosaic cells, tiles, hidden characters, or the strokes of a giant word and their cast shadows — and each touched region steps back down to the resting tone shortly after the light moves on, leaving only a short fading wake. Fits requests for spotlight and torch reveals across dark pages, cell or tile grids that light up and fade under a hover sweep, backlit walls whose glow follows the cursor, and lamp-over-typography scenes whose shadows re-aim as the light roams, where the content is revealed or lit but never changed.

self_running_pulse_wave_field.name: self_running_pulse_wave_field
self_running_pulse_wave_field.description: A field of evenly repeating elements or soft light sitting behind ordinary content and carrying a slow calm rhythm of its own: concentric rings, waves or breathing swells travel outward across the lattice and settle back toward a resting level, running endlessly without the visitor and at most seeded from the point of a press, while the foreground content stays completely undisturbed. Fits requests for pulsing dot or block grids, radiating wave and ripple backdrops, quietly breathing glow fields behind a single action, and press-rippled ambient surfaces, where the rhythm is ambient and self-restoring rather than something the visitor steers or draws.

falling_glyph_column_curtain.name: falling_glyph_column_curtain
falling_glyph_column_curtain.description: A full-bleed surface densely filled with vertical columns of small characters falling at clearly differing speeds and lengths, each column headed by its brightest glyph while the characters behind it dim, flicker between shapes and dissolve before reaching the bottom; it begins already running, never stops, reflows to any window size without a seam, and any visitor response is limited to individual columns flaring as the pointer passes. Fits requests for glyph rain, code-rain and character downpour backdrops, digital-rain hero and section fills, and text-curtain surfaces whose interest is the endless descent of characters behind or around ordinary content.

switchable_mood_recolored_light_field.name: switchable_mood_recolored_light_field
switchable_mood_recolored_light_field.description: A softly drifting or rippling light surface behind readable content whose motion never pauses, paired with one deliberate command — a tap anywhere or a single control — that snaps the entire field into a different colour atmosphere while the drift continues unbroken, with no palette fixed in advance. Fits requests for animated gradient, glow or tinted-tile backdrops with a colour-mood or theme switch, hero surfaces where tapping repaints the whole scene, and mood-cycling ambient fields whose only interaction is choosing which atmosphere the surface wears next.

travelling_depth_scene_backdrop.name: travelling_depth_scene_backdrop
travelling_depth_scene_backdrop.description: A scene with real depth used as the setting for still wording, where the camera keeps moving: terrain, streaks, structures or stacked scene layers travel endlessly toward the viewer, or the whole layered picture re-aims with pointer movement and device tilt so near parts shift further than far ones, and a press, drag or tilt only speeds, widens or leans the view before it eases back to its calm cruise or resting centre. Fits requests for endless flythrough and light-rush heroes, looping landscape or valley glides, layered parallax scenes that lean with the cursor, and cinematic pull-back openings that settle into a deep framed view holding a short title.

pointer_tracked_inplace_image_response.name: pointer_tracked_inplace_image_response
pointer_tracked_inplace_image_response.description: One picture is held in place as the whole subject and the pointer is the only control: as the cursor or a device tilt travels across it the image itself responds continuously — its parts separating into apparent depth planes, its plane of sharpness sweeping, its frame leaning, or its surface breaking into cells, tiles and smears that lag behind the cursor and reach further the faster it moves — and it eases back to the plain, undistorted, composed picture once the pointer stops or leaves. Nothing is advanced or navigated; the mechanism is a reversible, self-healing transformation of the standing image and drops onto any single image. Fits requests for photos that gain depth or parallax under the mouse, hover-driven focus, lens or blur effects on one picture, cursor-trailing pixel, tile, mosaic or smear distortion, and image heroes that come alive on pointer movement and settle flat at rest.

focus_slot_image_run_with_reactive_surro.name: focus_slot_image_run_with_reactive_surround
focus_slot_image_run_with_reactive_surro.description: A continuous run or ring of images is moved by weighted drag, flick, wheel or key input with momentum, damping and snapping, and whichever item reaches the fixed focal slot is promoted to full clarity, size, colour or luminance while neighbours on both sides step down yet stay visible so the set reads as continuing. The surround reacts to whatever currently holds focus, borrowing its colour or otherwise re-lighting the stage and blending partway toward the neighbour in proportion to the pull, snapping back if the pull is released short and completing when the step lands; a chosen item may be carried out of its slot into a fullscreen or detail view and carried back into the exact slot it left. Fits requests for centred carousels and coverflow-style rows or rings where the middle item is the active one, momentum sliders whose focused picture drives the background colour or ambience, and browsable image runs where selecting the focused item opens it and returns it to place.

enclosing_image_volume_flight.name: enclosing_image_volume_flight
enclosing_image_volume_flight.description: Images are mapped onto a curved three-dimensional structure that surrounds the viewpoint — a concave ring, an encircling band, a receding shaft or tunnel — and input moves the viewer or the structure through that space: scrolling flies the camera toward, over, inside and back out of the volume, dragging spins it endlessly with inertial coasting, and whatever faces the viewer reads at full strength while the rest curve away and fade. The surround stays bare and unadorned so the constructed space is itself the arrangement. Fits requests for tunnel, cylinder, ring or carousel-in-space image experiences, scroll-driven camera flights through a wall of pictures, spinning picture rings dragged around the viewer, and immersive collection views where the images build the room.

overview_to_single_image_zoom_transit.name: overview_to_single_image_zoom_transit
overview_to_single_image_zoom_transit.description: A regular grid or wall holding the whole collection and one image owning the entire screen are the two ends of a single continuous, exactly reversible transit, and one input drives the layout along it: scroll progress pins and magnifies the tiles until one fills the view, or a click grows the chosen tile out of its own slot while the remaining tiles clear off-frame in the direction they sit. The layout keeps its identity throughout, with no cross-fade to a separate page, and reversing retraces the identical path back to the overview. Fits requests for pinned scroll zooms into an image grid, tile walls that open into a featured picture, gallery grids where clicking a thumbnail expands it to fullscreen and clicking again puts it back, and overview-to-detail collection transitions carried by one continuous zoom.

scattered_depth_preview_field_with_promo.name: scattered_depth_preview_field_with_promoted_detail
scattered_depth_preview_field_with_promo.description: A collection is laid out as a loose, dimmed scatter of preview images at mixed depths in a quiet surround, held as atmosphere rather than as final content: pointer movement or dragging glides and tilts the whole field for parallax, the entry under focus lifts, leans, brightens, gains full colour or is named, and choosing it promotes that entry into its own full-strength view — one photo taking the whole screen, or the entry's pictures gathering into a composed readable arrangement — while the rest of the field is swept aside, dimmed or blurred; dismissing collapses back into the untouched scatter at the place it left. Fits requests for floating or scattered photo fields that parallax under the cursor, project and collection indexes with faint teaser images behind big names, hover-lifting depth galleries, and preview scatters that open into a detail or gallery view and return to the field.

stepped_fullframe_image_handoff.name: stepped_fullframe_image_handoff
stepped_fullframe_image_handoff.description: One image fills the frame as a still resting state with its wording set large over it, and a discrete previous/next step runs a self-contained handoff: the standing picture breaks into facets, tiles, quarters or abstract pieces, flings out or dissolves, the next picture arrives and eases or springs into the new resting place, and the accompanying title performs its own matching exit and entrance in step. Each step is a one-shot timeline with a fixed start and a fully composed, motionless end; there is no continuous scrubbing of position and no promotion into a different layout. Fits requests for fullscreen photo steppers and hero sliders with dramatic transitions, shatter, slice, dissolve or pixel-break image swaps, one-picture-at-a-time showcases with large captioned names, and full-bleed captioned carousels advanced by arrows, keys or buttons.

scroll_scrubbed_image_descent.name: scroll_scrubbed_image_descent
scroll_scrubbed_image_descent.description: Downward travel is the clock for a long single-column image sequence: each picture's state is a function of how far it has moved through the view, arriving out of blur, coarseness, desaturation, an edge wipe, a steep tilt or the body of the one before it, reaching full sharpness and presence in the focal band, then softening, stretching, tipping or dissolving away as it leaves, while captions, numbers, titles or oversized names arrive and travel in the same proportion; pushing back up unwinds every stage exactly. Fits requests for cinematic scroll-through photo essays and editorial image sequences, scroll-driven reveal or resolve effects down a gallery page, smooth momentum descents through a portfolio one large picture at a time, and quiet vertical showcases where the type moves in step with the pictures.

embodied_avatar_roaming_place.name: embodied_avatar_roaming_place
embodied_avatar_roaming_place.description: The visitor is present in the place as a visible figure they steer, holding a direction or picking a spot on the floor to walk wherever they like while the view trails behind, and the surroundings answer both the steps and the figure's presence: ground marked or bent underfoot, nearby structure resolving as it is approached, a typed line hovering over the head, an overview corner to stay oriented. Nothing is laid out to follow, so releasing the controls simply leaves the figure standing where it stopped and it can set off again in any direction. Fits requests for walkable worlds, plains, fields, rooms and interiors wandered as a character, third-person avatar exploration, inhabited places where a little figure moves and lingers among others, and any place whose point is free self-directed movement by a body the visitor can see, rather than a viewpoint carried along a laid-out route, a scene leaned under the pointer from one vantage, a destinationless cruise, or a field of points flown between.

endless_steered_cruise_through_open_spac.name: endless_steered_cruise_through_open_space
endless_steered_cruise_through_open_spac.description: The surroundings stream continuously past a viewpoint or craft that stays fixed in the frame, travelling on forever with nothing to arrive at: motion runs by default or builds and falls away under held keys, and the visitor only leans, steers or throttles it while depth ahead and behind dissolves into haze or featureless void. Letting go never ends the journey, it only lets the travel settle back toward its resting drift, and no part of the route is marked out or stopped at. Fits requests for endless flights and cruises, corridors and tunnels rushing past the viewer, drifting aerial or tilted overhead expanses, craft and vehicle travel over open terrain, and any place whose whole content is the sensation of continuous passage, rather than a figure walked about, a route scrubbed to a fixed ending, stops that hold travel for reading, a scene inspected from one vantage, or points chosen out of a cluster.

scroll_scrubbed_route_flight_into_scene.name: scroll_scrubbed_route_flight_into_scene
scroll_scrubbed_route_flight_into_scene.description: Scrolling drives the viewpoint along one predetermined path through a place, scroll position standing in for position on the route: the place resolves out of distance or haze, travel turns and pushes toward whatever the path leads to, it eases to a hold wherever scrolling stops, and it rewinds through the identical path when scrolled back, coming to rest in a final frame instead of continuing. Fits requests for scroll-piloted flythroughs, cinematic descents and approaches into a city, village or landscape, scroll-scrubbed camera tours that turn to face each landmark, and any place travelled as one governed pass under the visitor's scroll, rather than roamed as a figure, cruised endlessly with no end, held at stations for reading, leaned under the pointer from a fixed vantage, or flown between chosen points.

guided_route_ride_past_in_scene_beats.name: guided_route_ride_past_in_scene_beats
guided_route_ride_past_in_scene_beats.description: The visitor is carried along one laid-out route past a run of small scenes, props and figures that swell into focus, act as they are passed, and slide away behind, with whatever is to be said carried inside the scenery itself and often a companion or character making the trip alongside. Travel never breaks off into a separate reading step: each beat happens on the way through, and the route either curls seamlessly back on itself for another pass or eases into a closing stretch. Fits requests for scrolling journeys and rides through a themed world, side-scrolling runs past dated milestones, miniature diorama tours, mascot-accompanied travelling scenes, and any route whose stops are performances passed in transit, rather than places where travel holds for a readable panel, a figure freely roamed, an endless destinationless cruise, a bare camera pass into a scene, or a field of points flown between.

stationed_walkthrough_with_reading_stops.name: stationed_walkthrough_with_reading_stops
stationed_walkthrough_with_reading_stops.description: Movement through the place is organised into stops: reaching a room, hall or marked spot holds travel while a caption or panel settles in to be read, and dismissing it or stepping on again releases the hold and carries the visitor to the next stop, the sequence cycling rather than finishing. The stops are situated in the surroundings themselves, so choosing one is choosing a place to stand. Fits requests for gallery and exhibit walkthroughs, room-to-room tours, showrooms and museum halls with captions, routes whose lit or pulsing markers pause travel to open text, and any place whose progression is stop, read, continue, rather than uninterrupted passage, free roaming as a figure, an endless cruise, or hotspots picked out of one fixed scene.

pointer_leaned_scene_with_hotspot_cards.name: pointer_leaned_scene_with_hotspot_cards
pointer_leaned_scene_with_hotspot_cards.description: One place is held whole in the frame and leans a few degrees toward the pointer so it reads as a real space being looked around from a single vantage; hovering names or marks the few things in it worth attention, selecting one brings that thing forward, the scene stilling while a framed card rises or the view carrying smoothly into that corner of the picture, and dismissing restores the whole place to life exactly as it was. Fits requests for interactive illustrated scenes, shoppable or furnished rooms whose pieces can be examined, scene-as-menu homepages whose entries are objects and nooks inside the picture, and any place looked over and picked at from a governed vantage, rather than travelled as a route, roamed as a figure, cruised endlessly, or held as stations along a walkthrough.

node_field_overview_to_focus_flight.name: node_field_overview_to_focus_flight
node_field_overview_to_focus_flight.description: Many small discrete points sit spread through a depth-graded space and together read as one structure the visitor can turn, pull nearer and push away at will; hovering lifts and swells the ones that lead somewhere, choosing one flies the viewpoint smoothly inward until that point and its immediate relations are framed beside a short readable summary, and a return flight restores the overview untouched. Fits requests for explorable idea maps and knowledge constellations, glowing point clouds and connected node structures browsed in depth, and overview-to-detail spatial navigation of a set of items, rather than a depicted locale walked as a figure, ridden along a route, cruised endlessly, or leaned under the pointer as one scene.

pointer_trailing_cursor_follower.name: pointer_trailing_cursor_follower
pointer_trailing_cursor_follower.description: The pointer itself is the animated object: the system cursor is replaced or shadowed by one or more soft marks, dots, rings, ribbons or full-length crosshair lines that chase the real pointer with springy lag, then smear, stretch, tear, fray, loop or overshoot in proportion to travel speed and direction and relax back to a clean resting shape whenever motion slows or stops, while the page underneath keeps its ordinary state apart from small reactions as the follower nears something clickable. Fits requests for custom cursors, cursor trails and pointer followers, gooey, elastic, liquid, rubbery or torn pointer marks, tapering trailing ribbons, stacked lagging rings, and crosshair or aiming reticles that track the pointer, wherever the payoff is the pointer stand-in's velocity-driven deformation and settling rather than any change to the thing being pointed at.

hover_drawn_stroke_on_word_entry.name: hover_drawn_stroke_on_word_entry
hover_drawn_stroke_on_word_entry.description: Pointing at one entry in a set of oversized words or names draws a fresh mark over that entry — an underline, stroke, slash or scribble — which arrives rough, hand-made, warped or noisy and then settles into a held clean shape, stays while the pointer remains, and retracts or hides when it leaves, with the entry's own lettering optionally shifting into an accent treatment and every other entry staying completely calm; nothing new is revealed beyond the mark. Fits requests for hover underlines, strikes and sketched hand-drawn marks on large type links, per-entry distortion character across a screen-filling name, index or menu list, and any list whose payoff is the mark drawn on the hovered word itself.

hover_revealed_item_payload.name: hover_revealed_item_payload
hover_revealed_item_payload.description: Pointing at or dwelling on one item in an otherwise calm set — a name in a text index, a marked word in running copy, a labelled tile, icon or object in a row — brings out that item's own concealed payload: its photograph, caption, definition panel, quote bubble, the contents held inside it or the pages within it. The payload springs, builds, tumbles or fans in beside the item or pinned at the pointer, may trail and tilt with further pointer movement, the rest of the set stays inert, and everything reverses or snaps shut when attention moves away, replaying on return. Fits requests for hover image previews on a name or project list, cursor-pinned or cursor-chased thumbnails, hover tooltips, glossary and explanation panels that assemble at the pointer, speech or quote bubbles popping from a word, and containers, boxes, books or folders that open on dwell to show what is inside or a link hidden within.

persistent_two_state_switch.name: persistent_two_state_switch
persistent_two_state_switch.description: One prominent control carries a real two-state condition that persists after the interaction: a press, tap or flip moves it into its other state and holds it there, announced by the control's own body — knob travel, outline morphing into the opposite symbol, tint and rim change, inner glow, opaque parts sliding aside — and often by the surrounding stage brightening, dimming or settling to match, with springy dip, overshoot, wobble or a brief celebratory burst dying away as it comes to rest ready to be flipped back. Fits requests for light switches, on/off and dark-mode style toggles, switch clusters, and oversized two-state icon or checkbox controls given a satisfying flip, wherever the payoff is a single control that visibly remembers which state it is in.

self_extinguishing_button_burst.name: self_extinguishing_button_burst
self_extinguishing_button_burst.description: A single unmistakably pressable button rests quietly until it gains attention, then erupts on and around its own body — arcs of light tearing along its edge, stray specks rushing inward and concentrating, its surface lifting in luminance, its emblem swelling, its label switching to active wording — after which the burst dies away by itself or springs back to the resting arrangement when engagement ends, leaving no state behind and no other element changed. Fits requests for hover and press effects on a call-to-action, submit or link button, electric, charging, magnetic or particle-gathering button reactions, and any button demo whose whole payoff is the momentary flare that decays back to calm.

exclusive_choice_marker_travel.name: exclusive_choice_marker_travel
exclusive_choice_marker_travel.description: A set of options laid out together in which exactly one is active: choosing another carries the active treatment across to the picked option — a highlight pill gliding and stretching to its width, a lens or trail bending the backdrop on the way, bars flying in to charge the new panel edge to edge, an outer glow and label tone switching on — while the previously chosen option gives its state back and drains to empty, and the arriving marker settles with a springy overshoot. Fits requests for tabs and segmented controls, radio-style pickers, plan, pricing and filter selectors, and option or setting rows whose payoff is the selection visibly travelling from the old pick to the new one.

opening_navigation_overlay_takeover.name: opening_navigation_overlay_takeover
opening_navigation_overlay_takeover.description: A trigger — a corner word, icon, strip or toggle — opens a navigation surface over the page: a panel, full-view field, thickened frame or enveloping backdrop arrives with its own elastic, cascading, sinking, widening or inward-growing entrance, the page behind is dimmed, veiled or made inert while staying in place, and the destination labels or icons land one after another in order; activating the trigger again, choosing a destination or pressing the covered area reverses the whole sequence. Fits requests for menu open and close animations, hamburger and corner-trigger overlays, side and edge drawers, full-screen menu takeovers, icon rails growing in from the window edges, and any navigation whose payoff is the staged arrival and withdrawal of the menu surface over unchanged content.

text_entry_focus_and_submit_feedback.name: text_entry_focus_and_submit_feedback
text_entry_focus_and_submit_feedback.description: A text field or compact form answers what is being done inside it: light or a small accent marker follows the caret or glides to whichever field holds attention and settles with a soft overshoot, a confirmation tick strokes itself in as an entry becomes acceptable, and committing a line breaks the typed characters apart and sweeps them away before the field empties, retakes focus and waits for the next one, sinking back to a quiet rest when the field is left. Fits requests for input focus and caret effects, glowing or reactive form fields, inline validation marks that draw themselves, and send, submit or clear feedback on a single-field composer, search or chat box, wherever the payoff is the field's own reaction to typing, focus and submission.

sheet_turn_page_readers.name: sheet_turn_page_readers
sheet_turn_page_readers.description: A sheet-like surface carrying one unit of content is physically turned, peeled or curled aside under a drag or a step so the adjacent unit is uncovered in its place, with the fold, curl or deepening shadow showing how far the turn has travelled, short pulls springing back untouched, and the ends of the run resisting instead of advancing; what the visitor tracks is the reading position moving one sheet at a time. Fits requests for book, magazine, brochure and bound-volume readers, page-turn and page-peel spreads, corner-drag and swipe-to-turn scene or chapter readers, and any paged reading experience whose changeover is the sheet itself being lifted over to reveal the next page.

single_word_screen_kinetic_decks.name: single_word_screen_kinetic_decks
single_word_screen_kinetic_decks.description: One oversized word or very short phrase owns an entire uniform field and is the performing subject there, animating on its own or letter by letter, and stepping or scrolling exchanges it for the next word together with its ground, type and quality of movement, forwards and backwards without end. Fits requests for kinetic typography showcases, one-word-per-screen scroll rides, type specimen and poster decks, self-demonstrating words that act out what they mean, and any page whose payoff is a succession of full-screen word states each carrying its own motion character.

scroll_resolved_giant_word_statements.name: scroll_resolved_giant_word_statements
scroll_resolved_giant_word_statements.description: A huge word or short statement begins spatially broken — formless noise, coarse blocks, offset slices or pulled-apart fragments — and scroll progress carries it into exact register and full legibility on a quiet ground, commonly alternating with small readable passages, with the resolved wording left standing once it lands and reversing only if you scroll back. Fits requests for scroll-driven headline assembly, condensing or clarifying keyword poems, mosaic and block build-up statements, sliced or ghosted giant type that sharpens when movement stops, and scroll-told word sequences whose payoff is illegible-to-legible resolution.

focal_line_text_restatement.name: focal_line_text_restatement
focal_line_text_restatement.description: A single held focal slot of type is restated in place: its characters churn through wrong forms and settle into the intended wording, or the next line takes over the very same centred position while neighbouring lines sit paler and unresolved, driven by an advance, a toggle, a hover or a scroll nudge, and the slot is always left readable and can be replayed or reversed. Fits requests for scramble, decode and glitch-resolve headlines, letter-by-letter text swaps and state or language toggles, line-by-line steppers and cryptic line processions, phrase columns that complete a fixed lead line, and any quiet screen whose subject is one line of text changing its wording where it stands.

travelling_edge_dual_state_compare.name: travelling_edge_dual_state_compare
travelling_edge_dual_state_compare.description: Two versions of one subject occupy a single frame and a travelling boundary — a crisp wipe, a ragged tear, a scrubbed seam — is driven across it by scroll or pointer position, so position on the drive maps directly to how much of each version is showing and the second state takes over the first, ending with the finished version in view. Fits requests for before-and-after comparisons, restoration, retouch and redesign reveals, wipe, sweep and curtain changeovers between two states of the same image, and scrub-controlled dual-state portraits.

depth_displaced_panel_stack_navigation.name: depth_displaced_panel_stack_navigation
depth_displaced_panel_stack_navigation.description: The full-view surface holding the current content is displaced in depth — sinking back, tipping aside, shrinking away or piling up — so the set it belongs to becomes visible as a receding or accumulating stack, with exactly one member held in the readable front position while scroll position or a press decides which; the movement is reversible and the falloff in scale, contrast or luminance shows where in the set you stand. Fits requests for stacked full-screen chapters and sections, cards that stack or recede as you scroll, depth overviews and section pickers that pull back from the page, tilt-aside menu reveals, and collections read one full panel at a time.

element_expands_to_full_frame_state.name: element_expands_to_full_frame_state
element_expands_to_full_frame_state.description: One focal element — a cover image, a far-off hero, a listing teaser — grows continuously from small or inset until it fills the whole frame and becomes the full state to read, while the surroundings part, fade or clear away, and the same drive can carry it back down to where it started. Fits requests for scroll-expanded covers and headline-parting intros, depth dives that pull a distant image forward into a sharp hero, teasers that open in place into a solitary full-story view, and any transition whose payoff is a small element taking over the entire screen.

on_cue_disintegration_into_particles.name: on_cue_disintegration_into_particles
on_cue_disintegration_into_particles.description: On an explicit cue, a solid authored element is broken into many small pieces — shards, blocks, specks, debris — that scatter or drift out of the frame, and the state left afterwards is the payoff: bare quiet ground, the message that was standing behind it, or the next form the pieces regather into, with the whole effect restorable and replayable. Fits requests for shatter, crumble, explode and dissolve-into-particles moments, unwrap-and-burst reveals, greetings uncovered by a breaking panel, and wordmarks that gather from or disperse into drifting particles.

sound_driven_reactive_visual_field.name: sound_driven_reactive_visual_field
sound_driven_reactive_visual_field.description: One full-view visual field whose behaviour is driven by playing sound: the page waits quiet, usually behind a single plain start cue, and from the moment the track begins the imagery pulses, swells, tears, blooms, glides or renews itself in step with the audio, typically separating heavy low-end weight from fine high-frequency detail so the sound-to-image link reads within seconds, and it keeps re-forming for as long as the audio runs instead of finishing; anything the visitor can do - moving the pointer, orbiting, zooming, holding a press - only tunes or re-reads that same sound-driven behaviour, and the picture slackens, stills or ends when the sound does. Fits requests for music visualizers and audio-reactive fullscreen scenes, beat-driven abstract or dimensional spectacles, click-to-start sound pieces whose cue clears exactly as the sound arrives, and long-running displays whose entire look is whatever is currently playing.

live_capture_mirror_field.name: live_capture_mirror_field
live_capture_mirror_field.description: One full-view field that takes the live camera feed as its only material and rebuilds whatever is in front of the screen out of discrete elements - dots, specks or points of light whose size, relief, brightness or hue follows the captured image - on a quiet uniform ground, so the content is the visitor's own face, body and gestures read back through the pattern, updating continuously as they move and collapsing to bare ground wherever there is nothing to read. Fits requests for webcam mirrors and live self-portraits, dot, halftone or character-grid camera views, and installation-like pages that turn whoever is watching into the picture.

pointer_attending_creature_character.name: pointer_attending_creature_character
pointer_attending_creature_character.description: One lifelike creature, character, mascot or little being alone in a quiet, nearly empty setting, idling with its own breathing or wandering until it attends to the visitor: its eyes, head, body or whole travelling path turns toward and pursues the pointer with a trailing lag and a soft overshoot, it holds its last heading or eases back to rest when the pointer stops, and a direct click or tap earns one short reaction before it settles again. Fits requests for cursor-following characters and mascots, eyes or faces that watch and track the visitor, pet-like creatures that chase, grip or can be poked, and quiet companion scenes whose whole point is that something alive notices where you are.

self_repairing_wordmark_material.name: self_repairing_wordmark_material
self_repairing_wordmark_material.description: A short word, name, phrase, logo or pair of marks is the subject, standing alone on a quiet near-empty field and made of loose-behaving material - thousands of specks, grains or points of light, or a solid surface that comes apart like one - shimmering, streaming or drifting on its own; sweeping or dragging the pointer through it locally scatters, tears open or hollows out only the touched part with a brief flare of brightness or colour, and the displaced material returns to its exact places, so the mark keeps healing and is never left illegible. Fits requests for particle text and logo intros, interactive typographic hero or cover panels, and word or mark treatments that break apart under the cursor and reassemble themselves.

pointer_disturbed_settling_substance_fie.name: pointer_disturbed_settling_substance_field
pointer_disturbed_settling_substance_fie.description: An edge-to-edge body of simulated stuff - liquid, goo, heat, flame, grain or similar continuous material - owns the view and sits in a calm resting state; the pointer is the energy source, so pressing and dragging shoves, flings, plows, paints or ignites the material exactly where it goes and holding drives the whole field harder, after which the disturbance spreads, drains, cools or slumps and the material relaxes back to rest, ready to be stirred again. Fits requests for fluid, water and goo playgrounds, smearable sand, paint or slime, fire and heat brushes, cursor-as-substance toys, and tactile full-screen simulations whose appeal is poking a material and watching it recover.

endlessly_self_morphing_quiet_form.name: endlessly_self_morphing_quiet_form
endlessly_self_morphing_quiet_form.description: One soft form, mass or expanse on a plain, evenly toned ground reshapes itself slowly and endlessly - swelling, thinning, stretching, splitting, rejoining, drifting or re-forming - with no goal, no ending and nothing to complete; the visitor is a watcher, and at most a compact set of controls dials the look or proportions of the same continuing motion without restarting or resolving it. Fits requests for calm ambient loops and meditative abstract visuals, slow organic blobs and morphing shapes, drifting cloud, smoke or wash scenes watched for their own sake, and screensaver-like pages that simply keep going.

orbitable_staged_volume_or_heap.name: orbitable_staged_volume_or_heap
orbitable_staged_volume_or_heap.description: A dimensional subject stands on a plain staged ground, lit and softly shadowed, and carries on by itself - a volume forming, unfurling and renewing, or objects arriving from off-view and piling into a heap that keeps jostling or settles into a finished tableau - while the visitor's real handle is the vantage: dragging swings the view around it and zooming closes in within limits, the released vantage simply holds, and at most a light nudge, a freeze or a lean toward the pointer touches the subject without redirecting what it is doing. Fits requests for orbitable staged showpieces, volumetric smoke or plume scenes, falling and stacking object displays that come to rest, and soft-body heaps that can be circled, zoomed and inspected.

still_picture_unit_rerender_studio.name: still_picture_unit_rerender_studio
still_picture_unit_rerender_studio.description: A fixed picture that is handed over, chosen or already sitting there as a sample is rebuilt wholly out of repeated small units — typed characters, dots, cells, blocks or glowing screen points — while a panel of parameters such as coarseness or detail, unit set, tonal polarity and colour versus single tone repaints the entire rendering the instant any of them moves, leaving the visible frame to be copied, saved or captured. Fits requests for ASCII and glyph picture converters, halftone, dot, mosaic and retro-screen image renderers, photo stylisation and filter studios, and any page whose outcome is one supplied still redrawn from a tunable field of marks. Does not fit a picture that only exists while a camera keeps feeding it, a clip converted and played back in motion, or a surface marked by the visitor's own hand.

live_camera_unit_field_mirror.name: live_camera_unit_field_mirror
live_camera_unit_field_mirror.description: The visitor's own live camera view is the subject and exists only as a coarse field of repeated units — swelling discs, dots or typed characters against a plain ground — continuously following their motion so the face and gestures are read from the pattern alone, optionally tuned from a small side panel and optionally frozen to hold or keep one still frame before releasing back to the moving view. Fits requests for webcam ASCII mirrors, dot or halftone camera portraits, live selfie pattern effects and any page whose picture is regenerated frame after frame from an arriving camera feed rather than from a stored file.

clip_to_symbol_animation_conversion_stag.name: clip_to_symbol_animation_conversion_stage
clip_to_symbol_animation_conversion_stag.description: A moving clip is the input: one dominant stage first loops a worked example, then takes bundled or handed-over footage and shows it rebuilt entirely from repeated units while it keeps moving, governed by pass and playback controls such as rising progress, a running frame or position counter, run/hold, reset or discard back to the opening state, with the moving result recordable and takeable away. Fits requests for video-to-ASCII and video-to-pattern converters, animated glyph or dot playback stages, and any page whose outcome is footage re-rendered in motion with playback and export handling.

self_playing_pattern_zoom_reveal.name: self_playing_pattern_zoom_reveal
self_playing_pattern_zoom_reveal.description: Nothing is supplied and nothing is marked: a finished two-tone pattern rendering of one picture plays itself as an unhurried framing move that opens on the bare units at extreme close range, eases outward through intermediate texture, resolves into the whole readable image and begins again, offering at most pause, manual framing sweep, restart or a style swap at the held framing. Fits requests for self-running reveal loops, macro-to-whole zoom-outs, texture-resolving-into-picture demos and ambient generated-art showreels whose picture forms on a timed progression without visitor input.

freehand_medium_mark_making_surface.name: freehand_medium_mark_making_surface
freehand_medium_mark_making_surface.description: One empty surface fills the view and a pressed drag deposits marks that behave like a physical medium — grainy pencil passes, thick smearing pigment, a glossy drifting ribbon, bleeding wet ink, sparking filaments or a trembling scribble — with a visible tip, brush or cursor tracking the pointer and each deposited mark continuing to settle, spread, bloom or fade after the gesture ends. Fits requests for drawing and painting toys, sketch pads, ink and brush playgrounds, expressive stroke and trail experiments, and any page whose picture is laid down stroke by stroke under continuous pointer pressure.

tap_seeded_growing_element_field.name: tap_seeded_growing_element_field
tap_seeded_growing_element_field.description: A near-empty field answers each discrete tap by planting one new element at that exact spot, which then carries on by itself — climbing, sprouting, gliding, orbiting or rocking — and stays permanently, so repeated taps accumulate a crowd or tangle that keeps moving with no further input. Fits requests for click-to-plant gardens, tap-to-spawn particle, token or creature fields, seeded growth scenes and any page whose composition accrues from placed, self-animating pieces rather than from a continuously dragged mark.

dimensional_type_specimen_stage.name: dimensional_type_specimen_stage
dimensional_type_specimen_stage.description: Text itself is the generated object: live-typed words or a supplied specimen paragraph stand as dimensional letterforms with visible bulk that idle with a slow continuous swell or undulation, rebuild in place the instant characters or typesetting values change, and can be orbited and approached freely. Fits requests for three-dimensional or volumetric type demos, soft cloud or puffed lettering typing stages, extruded typography specimens and any page whose picture is the shape of the words being set rather than an image being converted or drawn.

typed_line_console_with_reacting_keys.name: typed_line_console_with_reacting_keys
typed_line_console_with_reacting_keys.description: Typing is the whole interaction: a depicted keyboard, terminal or writing machine takes keystrokes directly, each struck key visibly sinking and springing back while characters land on a pending line or sheet, and the text surface grows downward as submitted lines are echoed, answered or advanced. The state that matters is the accumulated transcript or page rather than any moving figure; work is committed one line at a time, heavier requests show a visible wait or ordered intermediate stages before a final outcome lands, and a single plain word or a fresh sheet returns everything to its opening state. Fits requests for command-line and terminal sessions, prompt-and-reply consoles, typewriter and text-entry pieces, oversized keyboard stages, and any page whose payoff is typing at a machine that reacts key by key and answers line by line.

simulated_screen_desktop_with_movable_pa.name: simulated_screen_desktop_with_movable_panes
simulated_screen_desktop_with_movable_pa.description: A whole screen or operating-system desktop stands in for the page: it may wake or boot first, then settle into a background carrying plainly named items, a strip that reports whatever is frontmost, and a row or shelf for launching, while content arrives as titled panes that overlap with exactly one clearly in front and can be dragged, resized, stacked, parked, expanded and closed inside the screen's own edges, keeping their contents for next time. Pointer motion, clicks and typing all go into the simulated machine, which redraws itself continuously as its own environment. Fits requests for fake desktops and OS shells, windowed workspaces, retro or scanlined computer screens presented as the whole page, and content or portfolio pages staged as a working computer being used.

faux_device_body_with_onboard_controls.name: faux_device_body_with_onboard_controls
faux_device_body_with_onboard_controls.description: One piece of hardware is rendered on the page — handheld, gadget, deck, player or machine console — and every input goes through the controls on its own body: direction pads, wheels, chunky keys and oversized buttons that visibly depress, clunk or sink into the housing under each press. The consequences stay inside the device: a small inset screen running its own session, reels or a disc turning, needles, counters and odometers advancing, tabs and side panels sliding out of the shell, and firm mechanical stops when something reaches an end. The device remains a self-contained object, so its session persists while it runs and resumes from where it stopped. Fits requests for playable handheld and console replicas, faux gadgets and appliances, tape decks, record and disc players, operable transports that run content under the visitor's commands, and pressable machine panels whose dials and readouts register every press.

seat_ringed_shared_turn_handoff_surface.name: seat_ringed_shared_turn_handoff_surface
seat_ringed_shared_turn_handoff_surface.description: One surface is shared by several people gathered around a device laid between them: each participant owns a zone, seat panel or marker on the rim, oriented to read upright from that person's own side, and exactly one of them holds the live turn. The holder is highlighted and is the only part that accepts input, a tap hands the turn on so the highlight, marker or whole central face moves round to the next seat, and every seat keeps its own visible running total, stake or remaining time while the rest sit dimmed. Rounds resolve with a plain verdict and roll straight into the next one, and a central hub or held control holds peeking, pausing and clearing. Fits requests for pass-and-play boards, shared-table and party games, per-seat scorekeepers, turn and game clocks, and any page where several people take turns at one screen between them.

pick_up_and_place_block_world_sandbox.name: pick_up_and_place_block_world_sandbox
pick_up_and_place_block_world_sandbox.description: A calm, low-distraction three-dimensional space with a readable ground plane is edited by hand: a held input aims at whichever discrete unit sits under the pointer or centre crosshair, takes it out of the world in visible stages or lifts it into the hand, and a release or open hand sets a unit back down solid against the surface or face it was aimed at. Carried units collect in a belt or inventory and the world simply keeps whatever has been done to it — no score, no timer, no failure state, only the accumulated arrangement. Fits requests for voxel and block sandboxes, dig-and-build loops, free-form construction spaces, and open-ended playgrounds where loose units are grabbed, carried and set down.

single_input_commit_attempt_with_full_re.name: single_input_commit_attempt_with_full_reset
single_input_commit_attempt_with_full_re.description: One minimal input — a tap, a press held exactly as long as needed, or a nudge of direction — is the entire control of an attempt that is already in motion: a piece sliding or falling toward a stack, a stick growing across a gap, a vehicle rolling toward a finish, a runner or craft carried forward past hazards and pickups. Each commit is judged immediately and visibly, success tightens the margin for the next one while pace, height or speed climbs, and a mistake collapses, wipes out or freezes the whole run so a single tap starts it again from exactly the opening state. Fits requests for one-button and hold-to-act games, stacking and spanning challenges, endless runners and flyers, timing and reflex tests, and short score-chasing interludes with instant retry.

steered_figure_bounded_arena_target_run.name: steered_figure_bounded_arena_target_run
steered_figure_bounded_arena_target_run.description: A bounded arena fills the view and the visitor steers one figure around inside it — aiming it with the pointer, sweeping the view to see what is closing in, or typing to pick off whatever is labelled. Targets keep arriving or reappearing, they burst and throw off feedback on contact or on a hit, momentum and the reach of the light or view limit what can actually be reached, and pressure rises as the crowd thickens. A drained meter or a catch ends the attempt with a summary and one-step retry, while goal-free variants just spring the next target up somewhere else. Fits requests for survival and wave arenas, top-down shooters and dodgers, chase-and-collect fields, typing-to-destroy games, and any page where a steered figure works one enclosed play space.

touch_excited_element_that_settles_back.name: touch_excited_element_that_settles_back
touch_excited_element_that_settles_back.description: The visitor touches the thing itself and it answers only where it was touched, then relaxes: sweeping a pointer or finger across a full-view medium raises crests, streaks or a wake that spreads, coasts and dissolves back into a flat resting field, and striking or pressing one piece of a kit or assembly makes that piece alone recoil, swing, flex or spring while sounding its own tone before settling to a ready rest. Nothing accumulates, nothing is scored and nothing can be lost, the element is always ready for the next touch, and holding while gliding across neighbours sets each of them off in turn. Fits requests for playable instruments and struck kits, ripple, ink and fluid surfaces that react to the cursor, pluckable or pressable object collections, and hands-on reactive materials whose whole payoff is disturbing them and watching them settle.

pointer_bent_surface_distortion.name: pointer_bent_surface_distortion
pointer_bent_surface_distortion.description: A continuous decorative field or membrane that deforms, swells, bends, or ripples outward from the pointer or press point and springs back to its resting state when the visitor leaves, while the foreground content stays legible above it. Fits requests for cursor-reactive bulging surfaces, ripple rings expanding from clicks, pointer-bending particle currents, soft swell fields, or press-origin waves traveling across a backdrop beneath calm text.

luminous_pointer_spotlight.name: luminous_pointer_spotlight
luminous_pointer_spotlight.description: A low-luminance decorative field where light, glow, or detail concentrates around the pointer as a moving lamp or breathing focus, illuminating nearby strokes or particles without mechanically bending the surface. Fits requests for a roaming spotlight over giant type, a glowing halo that follows the cursor through drifting particles, a breathing light gathering behind an action, or trailing luminous smears along the pointer path.

autonomous_drifting_atmosphere.name: autonomous_drifting_atmosphere
autonomous_drifting_atmosphere.description: A decorative atmospheric field of drifting points, haze, streaks, or fine texture that moves on its own in continuous currents, swirls, or flows, optionally reacting with a gentle local disturbance but defined by its endless self-driven motion rather than pointer tracking. Fits requests for slowly drifting dot fields, twin-swirl hazes, inward-gathering speck currents, converging signal funnels, receding depth vortices, streaming light rushes, drifting haze pockets, or snowfall layered over a photo.

text_as_material_volume.name: text_as_material_volume
text_as_material_volume.description: Large wording treated as a physical or optical material whose body is bent by glass volumes, revealed as cut-out windows into a living textured fill, assembled from scattered grains, or surrounded by chromatic afterglow ghosts, making the typographic form itself the decorated subject. Fits requests for glass-refracted phrases, thick volumes wrapping lettering, words cut out to show drifting interior textures, scattered light grains reassembling into names, or giant words with breathing chromatic echoes.

distressed_content_surface.name: distressed_content_surface
distressed_content_surface.description: An entire reading view rendered through a continuous visual degradation, instability, or malfunction effect applied uniformly across prose, photos, and interface elements, maintaining legibility while simulating a failing screen or weakened signal. Fits requests for degraded console reading decks, flickering and trembling prose-and-photo scrolls, or views carrying a uniform glitchy or unstable atmospheric treatment over all their content.

endless_linear_image_stream.name: endless_linear_image_stream
endless_linear_image_stream.description: Images travel continuously along a single axis — horizontally or vertically — as an unbroken drifting run, column, or depth passage that glides under drag, wheel, or fling input and loops or extends without end. Fits requests for infinite scrolling galleries, horizontal photo carousels, endless sideways image journeys, vertical photo columns, and forward-drifting depth streams where the primary mechanism is continuous linear traversal.

grid_field_with_pointer_focus.name: grid_field_with_pointer_focus
grid_field_with_pointer_focus.description: A two-dimensional spread of small peer images arranged in a uniform grid or open field whose salience, size, or chroma responds directly to pointer proximity or selection, swelling into focus at the cursor while the surround stays suppressed. Fits requests for thumbnail grids, interactive photo walls, magnetic image fields, hover-reveal galleries, and pointer-driven browsing collections where the causal kernel is cursor-following emphasis across a flat array.

card_deck_fan_and_reshape.name: card_deck_fan_and_reshape
card_deck_fan_and_reshape.description: Image cards gather into a resting pile or deck that fans, spreads, arcs, or reshapes into rings and columns on demand, with step-through browsing and reversible collapse back to the original stack. Fits requests for card-based galleries, fanning image decks, reshaping photo collections, and interactive card stacks where the causal kernel is physical stacking, fanning, and re-forming of discrete items.

counter_drifting_multi_column_wall.name: counter_drifting_multi_column_wall
counter_drifting_multi_column_wall.description: Multiple parallel vertical runs of images glide past each other in opposing directions during scroll, producing shearing parallax between adjacent columns while a centred focus state selects one item. Fits requests for multi-column parallax galleries, opposed-scroll image walls, staggered vertical photo grids, and shearing portfolio layouts where the causal kernel is differential vertical motion between neighbouring columns.

scatter_layered_takeover_gallery.name: scatter_layered_takeover_gallery
scatter_layered_takeover_gallery.description: Loosely scattered or stacked image layers rest across the full view, responding to pointer movement with differential drift or lift, and expanding to claim the entire screen on selection. Fits requests for scattered photo layouts, layered parallax galleries, fullscreen takeover image viewers, and overlapping card sets where the causal kernel is loose spatial distribution with pointer-reactive depth and single-item expansion.

single_image_transform_viewer.name: single_image_transform_viewer
single_image_transform_viewer.description: One image occupies the whole view and transitions to the next through material metamorphosis — dissolving, folding, melting, or fragmenting — directly tied to scrub or click input. Fits requests for single-photo viewers, artistic image transitions, dissolve slideshows, and full-screen photo sequences where the causal kernel is per-image transformation rather than spatial traversal of a collection.
